solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: State essentially giving rector restorable friary

indicators.note: the essence of each word is its core, so the central pair of letters is taken from each of the four words

explanation.surface: A rector is handed a friary that could be restored to its former glory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' applies to all four words: the middle two letters of giving, rector, restorable and friary, joined in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria is one of the six states of Australia.

clue.text: He comes into estate to sort out their iron

indicators.note: to sort out letters is to put them into a new order, so the words their iron are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new landowner arrives at his estate and tackles the ironwork there.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is someone who comes into, or inherits, an estate.

clue.text: What you're looking at — a prosperous part of England

definitions.meaning: the things right in front of you, pointed to as near at hand
the South East, England's wealthiest region, abbreviated SE with the article before it

explanation.surface: A pointed remark about a wealthy English region on view.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as THE SE: the South East, the London-centred region of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstrative pronoun pointing to nearby objects, the ones currently in view.

clue.text: They measure exposure to nasty green snot

indicators.note: something nasty is in a bad state, so the letters of green snot are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Instruments detecting how much contact someone has had with unpleasant green mucus.
explanation.definitionFit: Units for measuring exposure to X-rays or gamma radiation, named after the physicist who discovered X-rays.

clue.text: Judge, stripped bare, nibbled the queen

indicators.note: stripped of its outer letters, so only the inner pair of the word bare stays

parts.note: nibbled means bit, past tense of bite
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A judge, naked, takes a bite out of the monarch: a courtroom scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone who settles disputes, acting as a judge between parties.

clue.text: Warning about Belgium's Einstein?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the warning word goes around the country's letter

parts.note: an alert is a warning
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: A warning delivered about Belgium's equivalent of a famous genius.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: one famous person with this first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert was Einstein's first name, so the physicist is one example of an Albert.

clue.text: School groups lose 150 fools

indicators.note: to lose something is to give it up, so these Roman numerals are taken out of the word

parts.note: classes are groups of pupils at a school
in Roman numerals C is 100 and L is 50

explanation.surface: School classes losing 150 pupils, leaving only the idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 150 in Roman numerals is CL; remove those two letters from CLASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Asses are stupid people, a common insult for fools.

clue.text: Old character taken in by telco set-up — they're not fair!

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the old letter goes within the telecoms company's initials

parts.note: BT, British Telecom, is the UK's main telecoms company
a rune is a letter of an old Germanic alphabet

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the word set runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written before the turn

explanation.surface: A historic figure duped by a phone company's scheme that isn't fair.
explanation.walkthrough: BT is British Telecom. 'fair' plays on just versus light-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunettes have dark hair, so they are not fair-haired: a pun on fair meaning just.

clue.text: Hands over worried predator

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the two hand letters go around the other piece

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left, a pair of hands
worried means ate, as in what is eating you

explanation.surface: Someone handing over a worried predator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands over' looks like a phrase meaning gives; split it. 'Worried' is ATE in the sense of troubled, as in what's eating you.
explanation.definitionFit: The honey badger, a fierce African and Asian carnivore, is a famous predator.

clue.text: Taps notice backing energy food

parts.note: C and H mark the cold and hot taps

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for notice is read backwards

parts.note: to notice is to see
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A notice backing energy food, read off by someone who taps the board.
explanation.walkthrough: Taps come in pairs marked C and H, for cold and hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese is a dairy product, a staple food eaten worldwide.

clue.text: Crackers pieces about one small copper

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for pieces is wrapped around the other letters

parts.note: bits are pieces
I is the Roman numeral one
S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Crackers broken into pieces worth about one small coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' looks like an adjective meaning mad; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers are a type of savoury biscuit, so plural nouns match.

clue.text: Determines position of sea otter in difficulties

indicators.note: something in difficulties is in disarray, so the letters of sea otter in are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Working out where a sea otter in trouble is located.
explanation.definitionFit: To orient oneself or something is to fix its position relative to the surroundings.

clue.text: Slippery customers were flush occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so every other letter of were flush is taken

explanation.surface: Untrustworthy people who were once rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are slimy, wriggly fish, and the phrase also means untrustworthy people.

clue.text: Force, in step, suffocate

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the force letter sits within the step word

parts.note: a stile is a step or set of steps over a fence
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: Applying force while marching in step until someone chokes.
explanation.walkthrough: A stile is a step for climbing over a fence or wall, common in the British countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle someone is to cut off their breath and smother them.

clue.text: Suddenly admits man's embarrassing situation

definitions.meaning: a door that bursts wide all at once lets people in
the zip of trousers undone, a familiar awkward moment

explanation.surface: A man suddenly confessing to an awkward predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: Flies is the British word for the zip opening on trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A door swinging wide lets things in; the trouser sense is a gaping zip.

clue.text: Maybe Ferdinand's holding very dry dishes

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the footballer's name goes around the other letters

parts.note: Rio Ferdinand is a former England footballer; maybe marks his first name as an example of a Ferdinand
so means very, as in so good
TT means teetotal, so dry in the sense of not drinking

explanation.surface: A footballer serving extremely dry plates of food.
explanation.walkthrough: Rio Ferdinand is a former England footballer. TT (teetotal) is a crossword stock for dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Risottos are Italian rice preparations, so each is an example of a dish.

clue.text: Display equipment is £1,000 less after climbing mushrooms

indicators.note: after means following, so the shortened equipment comes behind the mushrooms
in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the mushrooms are read from the bottom

parts.note: ceps are wild porcini mushrooms

indicators.note: less means minus, so the thousand letter is dropped

parts.note: tackle is gear or equipment, as in fishing tackle
K stands for a thousand, so a grand

explanation.surface: Climbing gear costing a grand less, on show beside some mushrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is an impressive public show or display.

clue.text: Fruit gone off before people look inside

indicators.note: off means gone bad, so the letters of gone are spoiled into a new order
inside means within, so the look word sits in the middle of people

parts.note: men are people
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit has gone rotten before anyone checks it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ogen is an Israeli melon variety; 'off' is the anagram signal, not 'gone off' as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, sweet melon variety with green flesh, first developed in Israel.

clue.text: German aristos could be sex party guests

indicators.note: could be means might be turned into, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Aristocrats from Germany who attend debauched parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgy participants are revellers at a wild party with sex.

clue.text: Covers Sarah Huckabee Sanders initially taking fierce criticism

indicators.note: taking means absorbing, so the initials go around the criticism
initially means at the start, so the first letter of each of the three names is taken

parts.note: heat is intense pressure or criticism, as in taking the heat

explanation.surface: A White House press secretary takes heavy flak while giving cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarah Huckabee Sanders was Donald Trump's press secretary, often under fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheaths are protective coverings, such as for a blade.

clue.text: English flower festival

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: An English flower show or festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian spring feast celebrating the Resurrection.

clue.text: Friends hit back

indicators.note: back means in reverse, so the word for hit is read from its end

parts.note: to slap is to hit

explanation.surface: Friends fighting back when struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Pals are close companions, an informal synonym.

clue.text: More competent constable redoubles arrests

indicators.note: arrests means holds, so the phrase constable redoubles captures the letters inside it

explanation.surface: A capable police officer doubles his arrest count.
explanation.definitionFit: Abler is the comparative of able, so more capable.

clue.text: Gross me out, somehow, with where relatives may sleep

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters of gross me out are rearranged

explanation.surface: A visitor complains the spare bedroom is disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare bedroom kept for visitors, where visiting family stay the night.

clue.text: See through poet's sauce

indicators.note: through means going in among, so the see letter lies inside the poet's name

parts.note: Thomas Gray wrote the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard
V stands for vide, Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: An instruction to examine a poet's recipe for sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: V (vide) is the Latin 'see' in footnotes; Thomas Gray was an 18th-century English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravy is a sauce made from meat juices.

clue.text: Flyer's a six-footer, head-to-toe

indicators.note: head to toe means the top letter goes to the bottom, so the first letter shifts to the end

parts.note: a louse is an insect, so it has six feet

explanation.surface: A very tall person is described, head to foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: An ousel or ouzel is a blackbird or similar bird, a creature that flies.

clue.text: Organised the Panel for Endangered Species

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so the letters of the panel are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A conservation panel set up to protect threatened wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Both African and Asian forms of this large mammal are listed as threatened with extinction.

clue.text: Investigation about fraudulent royal ends in Leeds?

definitions.note: a building of this kind found in Leeds, Kent, rather than the city

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the investigation word goes around the end letters

parts.note: a case is an investigation by police

indicators.note: ends means final letters, so the last letter of fraudulent and of royal are taken

explanation.surface: An inquiry into a fake royal ends in the city of Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds Castle is in Kent, England, not the northern city; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds Castle is a famous medieval fortress in Kent, so this is the kind of building in Leeds.

clue.text: Fail to start job, longing to return to islands

indicators.note: fail to start means losing the opening letter, so the job word loses its first letter

parts.note: work is a job

indicators.note: to return means going back, so the longing word is read backwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: Someone fails to start a job, longing to go back to the islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Orkney is an archipelago off the north coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Ants held off My Little Pony

indicators.note: off means out of sorts, so the letters of ants held are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ants are kept away from a children's toy pony.
explanation.walkthrough: My Little Pony is a toy line; 'My' is an exclamation linking the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shetland is a small, sturdy pony breed from the Scottish islands.
